title: Where the aid goes

controls.label: Share spent on roads, schools and clinics

readouts.l: Shares: roads, schools, clinics / corruption / imports

predict.q: A country receives aid grants worth 5% of its GDP for one year. Almost all of it is spent on imported luxury goods for officials. What happens to the country's long-run productive capacity?

options.s: LRAS shifts right by about 5%, the size of the aid
options.fb: The size of the aid does not set the LRAS shift. Spending on imported luxuries adds nothing to future capacity.

options.s: LRAS barely moves: the aid adds nothing lasting to capacity
options.fb: Imported luxuries leave the economy: a small, passing AD blip (0.5%) and no LRAS shift.

options.s: LRAS shifts left, because the aid must be repaid
options.fb: These are grants: nothing is repaid. Spending them on luxuries wastes them, but does not shrink capacity.

options.s: The price level falls, because more goods are imported
options.fb: Imported luxuries leave AD and LRAS almost unchanged, so there is no reason for the price level to fall.

task: Move the "share spent on roads, schools and clinics" slider, and the "share lost to corruption" slider. Watch AD now and LRAS later.

target.do: Move the roads, schools and clinics slider up, then press Check.

takeaway: Aid raises long-run capacity only when it is spent on things that raise future output.
explore: Find the settings that shift LRAS furthest: all 10% of GDP on roads, schools and clinics, none lost.
